output.headline: General Atlantic brings a Physician Groups base, two Midwest deals and a 16.5x median price paid to this $200M Midwest target.
output.differentiator: Its edge is a growth-equity mandate that spans Healthcare [P:1], two prior Midwest deals [T:record] and a 16.5x median multiple paid, above the comparable 75th percentile of 15.3x [T:record, V:comps]. It lacks the open-platform add-on route of Nordic Capital, Welsh Carson and Advent [A:angles].

acquirer_overview.title: General Atlantic is a growth-equity sponsor with 14 deals since 2019 and a strong close rate
acquirer_overview.body: It describes itself as a growth equity firm investing across Technology, Consumer, Financial Services, Healthcare and Life Sciences [P:1]. AUM is US$125.3 billion in the infobox, but the body text says over $118 billion, so the sources differ [P:2]. It has 14 deals from 2019 to 2024; 13 closed and all 14 were control deals [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share]. The median deal is $158M [T:record]. Its home sub-sector is Physician Groups, with 4 deals [B:buyer, K:by_sub_sector]. It sits at Tier 1 position 4, with a likelihood of 4.5% across 107 buyers scored [R:rank].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: The fit rests on Physician Groups depth, Ring 1 breadth and a Midwest record, not an open platform
strategic_fit_thesis.body: Deals in this or neighbouring sub-sectors lift the odds by x1.11 [S:sector_rel]. It has 1 Core deal and 8 in Ring 1 [T:record]. The Core deal is Oak Health, a $1,708M merger of equals in 2021 at 18.8x [D:MA-2021-0066]. In Physician Groups it bought Crest Medical Practice, a $121M leveraged buyout in 2023 at 11.5x [D:MA-2023-0499]. It has 2 Midwest deals, including Harbor Home Health Partners, a $15M acquisition in 2022 at 16.9x [T:record, D:MA-2022-0273]. With no open platform, the target would be a standalone investment, not an add-on [A:angles].

precedent_activity.title: Recent precedents show closed sponsor deals near the target's size, plus one termination
precedent_activity.body: General Atlantic has done 4 deals since 2022, and 3 of 14 sit in the $100M-$400M size band [K:recent, K:size_band]. The closest is Crest Medical Practice: $121M in 2023 at 11.5x EV/EBITDA and 2.31x EV/Revenue [D:MA-2023-0499]. Reliable Medical Associates was $71M in 2021 at 13.8x [D:MA-2021-0392]. Frontier Clinics, a $7M platform investment in 2021, was terminated [D:MA-2021-0337]. Its close rate adds x1.12 to the odds [S:close_rate_s, K:closed_share].

valuation_context.title: Defend the 75th percentile on margin; General Atlantic's pricing supports it, but returns are tight at $200M
valuation_context.body: The 70 comparable deals show EV/EBITDA of 10.7x at the lower quartile, 12.8x at the median and 15.3x at the 75th percentile [V:comps]. The target's 16.8% margin beats the comps' median of 12.9% and exceeds 87% of comps, which supports the 75th [V:comps, X:target]. That needs $13.1M of EBITDA [V:comps]. General Atlantic's median paid is 16.5x [V:comps, T:record]. With 5.0x leverage at 8.5% and a $128M equity cheque, IRR at the ask is 18.7% against a 20% target [V:lbo].

risk_flags.title: Return gap at the ask
risk_flags.concern: IRR at the ask of 18.7% is below the 20% target, and the $193M maximum price on the same exit is below the $200M EV.
risk_flags.mitigant: A platform exit at 15.0x lifts the maximum price to $216M, above the $200M EV.
risk_flags.reality: The price works only if General Atlantic underwrites a platform exit at 15.0x; a same-exit case does not clear its target return [V:lbo].

risk_flags.title: No open platform, thin sub-sector share
risk_flags.concern: It has no open platform in the sub-sector, and its share of deals in the target's sub-sector is a signal against, at x0.98.
risk_flags.mitigant: It has 1 deal in the target's sub-sector and 8 in Ring 1, and neighbouring-sector deals add x1.11.
risk_flags.reality: The fit is by adjacency, not a bolt-on, while Nordic Capital, Welsh Carson and Advent all offer an add-on route [S:sector_share, S:sector_rel, C:conviction, A:angles].

risk_flags.title: Crowded sponsor process
risk_flags.concern: GTCR shares its provider-specialist and size-fit angles, and Welsh Carson adds an open platform to both.
risk_flags.mitigant: General Atlantic has 2 Midwest deals and a 16.5x median multiple paid, so it can compete on price.
risk_flags.reality: It is Tier 1 position 4 with model rank 7 and a likelihood of 4.5%, so it is not the front-runner [R:rank, T:record, A:angles].

conviction.rationale: The basis for conviction is 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector and 8 in Ring 1 (same business model). It is held at Medium because there is no open platform in the sub-sector [C:conviction].
